Vik: Short form of Viktor or Victor, from Latin 'conqueror'; also Scandinavian vik 'bay'. Probably a nickname.
Diego: Spanish, possibly a form of Santiago (James) or from Greek didache 'teaching'. Origin debated.
Lotte: Dutch and German short form of Charlotte, the French feminine of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Anas: Arabic, 'friendliness' or 'companionship'. Borne by a Companion of the Prophet.
Fatima: Arabic, possibly 'one who abstains' or 'captivating'. Daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.
Leonie: German and Dutch form of Léonie, feminine of Leon, from Latin leo 'lion'.
Simon: Greek form of Hebrew Shimon, 'he has heard'. Apostle Simon Peter.
Mauro: Italian and Spanish, from Latin Maurus 'Moorish' or 'dark-skinned'.
Flor: Flemish and Spanish, 'flower', from Latin flos; also short for Florent or Floris.
Ahmed: Arabic, 'most praised', from the root h-m-d. A name of the Prophet Muhammad.
Rafael: Spanish, Portuguese and German form of Raphael, Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Eloïse: French, probably from Germanic, possibly 'healthy' or 'wide'. Origin uncertain; famous via Héloïse and Abelard.
Thomas: Greek form of Aramaic te'oma, 'twin'. One of the apostles.
Mathieu: French form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Cas: Dutch short form of Casper or Cassius; Casper is probably Persian 'treasurer'.
Martin: From Latin Martinus, derived from Mars, the Roman god of war. Saint Martin of Tours.
Mathéo: French form of Matteo or Matthew, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Emilio: Italian and Spanish form of Aemilius, a Roman clan name possibly from 'rival'.
Muhammad: Arabic, 'praised' or 'praiseworthy'. Name of the Prophet of Islam.
Augustin: French form of Augustine, from Latin augustus 'venerable'. Saint Augustine of Hippo.
Remi: French form of Remigius, from Latin 'oarsman'. Saint Remigius baptised Clovis.
Alexandre: French form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Noa: Hebrew, 'movement' or 'comfort', feminine of Noah. Also used for boys in Spanish-speaking countries.
Idris: Arabic, a prophet of Islam, often explained as 'interpreter' or 'studious'. Also Welsh Idris 'ardent lord'.
Kobe: Flemish pet form of Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov. Also a Japanese city and Basque name.
Féline: French, 'feline' or 'cat-like', from Latin felinus. Also related to Latin felix 'happy'. Modern name.
Nova: Latin, 'new'. In astronomy a star that suddenly brightens; modern name.
Maxim: Russian and Dutch form of Maximus, from Latin 'greatest'.
Eliana: Hebrew, 'my God has answered'; also Latin and Greek 'sun' in some traditions.
Arya: Sanskrit, 'noble'. Popularised in the West by the Game of Thrones character.
Sam: Short form of Samuel, Hebrew 'name of God', or Samson.
Mateo: Spanish form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Issa: Arabic form of Jesus; also an African name in several languages. Meaning varies by origin.
Romain: French, from Latin Romanus, 'of Rome' or 'Roman'.
Livio: Italian from Latin Livius, a Roman clan name possibly 'bluish' or 'envious'. Livy the historian.
Jean: French form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'.
Marceau: French diminutive of Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, linked to Mars.
Alina: Possibly a short form of Adeline or Albina, or Slavic, Germanic 'noble'. Origin uncertain.
Aster: Greek, 'star', and the name of a flower. Also Amharic 'star' as Ester.
Floris: Dutch, from Latin Florus 'flowering'. Borne by medieval counts of Holland.
Romane: French feminine of Romain, from Latin 'Roman'.
Mathias: Variant of Matthias, from Greek form of Hebrew Mattityahu, 'gift of God'.
Timéo: French form of Timothy or Timaeus, from Greek 'honouring God' or 'honour'.
Abel: Hebrew, possibly 'breath' or 'meadow'. Second son of Adam and Eve.
Moussa: Arabic and African form of Moses, from Hebrew or Egyptian; 'drawn from water' per the Bible.
Félix: French and Spanish form of Felix, Latin 'happy' or 'lucky'.
Amber: English, from the fossil resin, from Arabic anbar. Used as a girls' name since the 19th century.
Tasnim: Arabic, a fountain in paradise, meaning 'raised up' or 'flowing from above'.
Maxime: French form of Maximus, from Latin 'greatest'. Used for boys and girls.
Elisabeth: Greek form of Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath' or 'God is abundance'.
Amalia: Germanic, from amal 'work'. Used in several languages.
Fien: Flemish short form of Jozefien or Josephine, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Yahya: Arabic form of John, 'God is gracious'. A prophet in Islam.
Roméo: French and Italian form of Romeo, 'pilgrim to Rome'. Shakespeare's lover.
Yara: Arabic, 'small butterfly' or 'friend'; also Tupi-Guarani 'lady of the waters'. Origin depends on culture.
Amélia: Portuguese and French spelling of Amelia, from Germanic amal 'work'.
Inès: French and Spanish form of Agnes, Greek 'pure' or 'chaste'.
Alex: Short form of Alexander or Alexandra, Greek 'defender of men'.
Théa: Greek 'goddess', or a short form of Dorothea or Theodora, meaning 'gift of God'.
Baptiste: French, from Greek baptistes 'baptiser'. John the Baptist.
Gabin: French, from Latin Gabinus, 'from Gabii', an ancient Italian town. Popularised by actor Jean Gabin.
Kaïs: Arabic Qays, possibly 'firmness' or 'measure'. Name of a famous poet in Arab tradition.
Ferre: Flemish short form of Ferdinand or Ferdi; Ferdinand is Germanic, 'bold journey' or 'protection'.
Alessio: Italian form of Alexis, from Greek alexios 'helper' or 'defender'.
Ayoub: Arabic form of Job, probably 'persecuted' or 'penitent'. A prophet in Islam.
Ellis: English, from Elias, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Also a Welsh surname.
Julian: Latin Julianus, from the Roman clan name Julius.
Fons: Flemish short form of Alfons, Germanic 'noble and ready'.
Lias: Probably a variant of Elias, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'; also a geological term. Origin uncertain.
Ida: Germanic id 'work' or 'labour'; also Greek, the nymph on Mount Ida. Origin disputed.
Auguste: French form of Augustus, from Latin 'venerable'.
Laura: Latin, from laurus 'laurel', symbol of victory. Immortalised by Petrarch's Laura.
Marilou: French, combination of Marie and Louise, or Marie and Lou.
Anastasia: Greek, 'resurrection', from anastasis. Popular in Orthodox countries.
Nore: Flemish short form of Eleonore or Honore; also possibly Scandinavian 'north'. Origin uncertain.
Hailey: English, from a surname meaning 'hay meadow', from Old English heg and leah. Modern given name.
Elina: Finnish and Greek, form of Helena, 'torch' or 'light'.
Antoine: French form of Anthony, from Latin Antonius, a Roman clan name of uncertain meaning.
Valentin: French and German form of Valentinus, from Latin valens 'strong' or 'healthy'.
Flore: French, from Latin flos 'flower'; Flora was the Roman goddess of flowers.
Aurora: Latin, 'dawn'. The Roman goddess of dawn.
Zakaria: Arabic form of Zechariah, Hebrew 'the Lord remembers'. A prophet in Islam.
Yusuf: Arabic and Turkish form of Joseph, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Emily: English, from Latin Aemilia, a Roman clan name possibly from 'rival'. Also linked to Germanic amal.
Younes: Arabic form of Jonah, from Hebrew 'dove'. A prophet in Islam.
Amelie: German spelling of Amélie, from Germanic amal 'work'.
Lya: Variant of Lia, short form of Leah or Julia. Origin uncertain.
Hector: Greek, 'holding fast'. Trojan hero in the Iliad.
Hannah: Hebrew Channah, 'grace' or 'favour'. Mother of the prophet Samuel.
Ralph: English, from Old Norse Raðulfr, 'counsel wolf'.
Kamiel: Flemish form of Camillus, a Roman family name possibly 'attendant of a religious rite'.
Nino: Italian and Georgian short name; in Italian a pet form of names ending -ino, such as Giovannino. Also a Georgian female name.
Mariam: Arabic and Armenian form of Mary, from Hebrew Miriam.
Dina: Hebrew, 'judged' or 'vindicated'; also Arabic 'religion'. Daughter of Jacob in the Bible.
Juul: Flemish form of Jules, from Latin Julius.
Otto: Germanic, from aud 'wealth' or 'fortune'. Borne by Holy Roman emperors.
Gabriël: Dutch form of Gabriel, Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Nicolas: French form of Nicholas, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Cleo: Short form of Cleopatra, Greek 'glory of the father'; also from kleos 'glory'.
Andreas: Greek and Dutch form of Andrew, from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'.
Agathe: French, from Greek agathos, 'good'. Saint Agatha.
Bilal: Arabic, 'moisture' or 'water'. First muezzin of Islam.
Elif: Turkish and Arabic, the first letter of the alphabet, alif; also 'slim'.
Thiago: Portuguese form of Tiago, from Santiago 'Saint James', Hebrew Yaakov.
Maxence: French, from Latin Maxentius, derived from maximus 'greatest'.
Aline: French, short form of Adeline, from Germanic adal 'noble'.
Fran: Short form of Frances or Francesca, Latin 'Frenchwoman' or 'free'.
Ines: Spanish and German form of Inés, from Agnes, Greek 'pure'.
Benjamin: Hebrew, 'son of the right hand' or 'son of the south'. Youngest son of Jacob.
Lisa: Short form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Bas: Dutch short form of Sebastiaan or Bastiaan, from Greek sebastos 'venerable'.
Rémi: French form of Remigius, from Latin 'oarsman'.
Pablo: Spanish form of Paul, from Latin Paulus 'small'.
Jef: Flemish short form of Jozef (Joseph), Hebrew 'God will add'.
Casper: Probably Persian, 'treasurer'. One of the three Magi.
Colette: French diminutive of Nicolette, from Nicholas, Greek 'victory of the people'.
Emir: Arabic, 'commander' or 'prince'. Used in Turkish and Bosnian.
Lyna: Variant of Lina, a short form of names ending in -lina; Arabic 'tender'.
Loua: Modern name, probably a variant of Lou or Louise; also Arabic. Origin uncertain.
Maëlle: Breton feminine form of Maël, from mael 'prince' or 'chief'.
Louisa: Latinised feminine of Louis, from Germanic 'famed warrior'.
Milou: Dutch and French pet name, possibly from Camille or Emilie, or Dutch pet form. Famous as Tintin's dog.
Florian: Latin Florianus, from florus 'flowering'. Saint Florian.
Luka: Slavic and Georgian form of Luke, from Greek 'man from Lucania' or 'light'.
Leyla: Arabic and Turkish, 'night'. Heroine of the classic Arabic love story Layla and Majnun.
Liyana: Arabic, 'soft' or 'tender'. Also used in Malay.
Émile: French form of Emil, from Latin Aemilius, a Roman clan name.
Elliot: English, from a surname derived from Elias, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Mya: Probably a variant of Mia or Maya; also Burmese 'emerald'. Origin uncertain.
Remus: Latin, twin brother of Romulus in Roman myth. Etymology uncertain.
Assia: Arabic, 'healer' or 'one who cares'; also the name of Pharaoh's wife in Islam.
Tobias: Greek form of Hebrew Tobiah, 'God is good'.
Oskar: German, Scandinavian and Polish spelling of Oscar, possibly Irish 'deer lover'.
Isra: Arabic, 'night journey', referring to Muhammad's journey to Jerusalem.
Mason: English, from the surname meaning stoneworker, from Old French masson.
Lyana: Variant of Liana or Lina; origin uncertain, possibly from French lier 'to bind' or Arabic 'soft'.
Lino: Italian short form of names ending in -lino, such as Carlino; also Greek 'linen'.
Wout: Dutch form of Wouter or Walter, Germanic 'army ruler'.
Leandro: Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Leander, Greek 'lion man' or 'man of the people'.
Cléo: French short form of Cléopâtre, Greek 'glory of the father'.
Margot: French diminutive of Marguerite, from Greek margarites 'pearl'.
Kasper: Scandinavian and Dutch form of Casper, probably Persian 'treasurer'.
George: English form of Greek georgos, 'farmer'. Saint George.
Stan: Short form of Stanley or Stanislaus; Slavic 'glory' and 'to become'. Also Dutch short form of Stanislas.
Edouard: French form of Edward, Old English 'wealth guardian'.
Emy: Variant of Emmy or Emi, short form of Emma or Emily. Probably Japanese 'beautiful blessing' in some uses.
Emil: Form of Aemilius, Roman clan name possibly from aemulus 'rival'.
Daan: Dutch short form of Daniel, Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Axel: Scandinavian, from Absalon, Hebrew 'father of peace'.
Alizée: French, 'trade wind', from alizé. Modern name popularised by a French singer.
Pippa: English, short form of Philippa, Greek 'lover of horses'.
Miran: Slavic, from mir 'peace' and an 'dear'; also used in Arabic and Armenian. Origin depends on culture.
Babette: French diminutive of Barbe or Élisabeth. Barbara is Greek 'foreign'; Elisabeth is Hebrew 'God is my oath'.
Elijah: Hebrew, 'my God is Yahweh'. Biblical prophet.
Anaïs: French and Catalan form of Anna, Hebrew 'grace'; also linked to Greek Anahita.
Alicia: Latinised form of Alice, from Germanic 'noble kind'.
Axelle: French feminine of Axel, from Absalon, Hebrew 'father of peace'.
Lenn: Probably a variant of Len, a short form of Leonard, Germanic 'brave lion', or of Lennart. Origin uncertain.
Sem: Dutch form of Shem, eldest son of Noah, Hebrew 'name'.
Magnus: Latin, 'great'. Made popular in Scandinavia after Charlemagne (Carolus Magnus).
Lucy: English form of Lucia, from Latin lux 'light'.
Capucine: French, 'nasturtium', literally a little hooded one; also from the Capuchin nuns. Rare girls' name.
Marie-Lou: French compound of Marie, from Hebrew Miriam, and Lou, from Louise (Germanic 'famed warrior').
Eli: Hebrew, 'ascent' or 'high'; also a short form of Elijah or Elias.
Muhammed: Arabic, 'praised'. Turkish and English spelling variant of Muhammad.
Noélie: French, 'Christmas', feminine of Noël, from Latin natalis 'birth'.
